lens: TAMRON 16-300mm F/3.5-6.3 Di II VC PZD B016
partial_phase_settings: 300 mm, f/40 (minimum aperture of the lens at that focal length), 1/4000 s, ISO 100
wide_frames: 16 mm, f/22, 1/4000 s, ISO 100 (two frames at 20:22)
clock_offset_method: Ordering constraint only. The corona sequence must lie inside totality, so the offset is bounded by [t_last - C3, t_first - C2]. No photometric model is involved, which is why it is robust; the area photometry was defeated by saturation blooming.
luminance_jump: Scene luminance normalised by ISO, exposure time and f-number rises by a factor 1600 between the last corona frame and the first post-eclipse frame at identical settings, and by 32x between two frames at IDENTICAL exposure (f/20, 1/250 s, ISO 800). That jump is third contact.

plate_scale_check.note: Independent confirmation of the optical chain: sensor pitch 3.717 um from the Canon spec, focal length 300 mm from EXIF, solar angular radius 946.66 arcsec from DE440s.

hot_pixels.caveat: No pre-eclipse baseline exists, so this is an absolute count and not a change. More important: the CW damage mode Schwarz et al. report is a LOSS OF RESPONSIVITY visible in flat fields, not a hot pixel in a dark frame. These images cannot test for it.

what_this_validates: the hardware modelled is the hardware used
totality lasted at least 41 s, consistent with the predicted 70.3 s
the observer shot the partial phases at f/40, far below the worst case modelled at f/6.3
what_this_does_not_validate: absolute contact times, because the camera clock was unsynchronised by about three minutes
the absence of responsivity loss, which needs a flat field
